{{Short description|French physicist and professor (1934–2015)}}
'''Marcel Froissart''' (20 December 1934, [[6th arrondissement of Paris]] –  21 October 2015, [[14th arrondissement of Paris]])<ref>[https://deces.matchid.io/id/E3xgYS-_IM2P Relevé des fichiers de l'Insee]</ref><ref name="CdF">{{cite web|url=https://www.college-de-france.fr/fr/personne/marcel-froissart|title=Marcel Froissart|website=Collège de France (www.college-de.france.fr)|date=11 April 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title = Monsieur Marcel FROISSART, avis de décès Paris(75) - Simplifia|url = https://www.simplifia.fr/avis-de-deces/marcel-froissart-paris|website = www.simplifia.fr}}</ref><ref name=dansnoscoeurs>{{cite web|url=http://www.dansnoscoeurs.fr/marcel-froissart/1559815/avis|title=Marcel Froissart - 80 ans|website=www.dansnoscoeurs.fr}}</ref> was a French theoretical physicist, specializing in [[particle physics]]. He is known for the [[Froissart bound]]<ref name=Polkinghorne>{{cite book | editor=DeTar, C. | editor2=Tan, C. | editor3=Finkelstein, J. | chapter=''Salesman of Ideas'' by John Polkinghorne|title=Passion For Physics, A: Essays In Honor Of Geoffrey Chew, Including An Interview With Chew | publisher=World Scientific Publishing Company | year=1985 | isbn=978-981-12-1920-7 | chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9LnVDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA23 | pages=23–25}}</ref> and the [[Froissart–Stora equation]].

== Biography ==
After secondary study at the [[Lycée Louis-le-Grand]], Marcel Froissart matriculated in 1953 at the [[École polytechnique (France)|École polytechnique]], where he graduated in 1955.<ref>{{cite web|title=Marcel Froissart (1934–2015)|website=annales.org|url=https://www.annales.org/archives/x/froissart.html}}</ref> He then entered in October 1956 Mines ParisTech, now known as [[Mines Paris - PSL|École nationale supérieure des mines de Paris (Mines Paris - PSL)]].<ref name=ParisTechstudents>{{cite web | title=Students of the École des mines de Paris corps des mines|url=https://www.annales.org/archives/eleves3.html|website=www.annales.org}}</ref> After completing only one semester of a four-semester technical curriculum, he was sent in civil cooperation with the French Navy to Algeria<ref>{{cite web|author=École des mines de Paris|language =en|title=Transcript of Marcel Froissart|url=https://www.annales.org/archives/images/n1/froissart.jpg|website=Annales.org}}</ref> (during the [[Algerian War]], which lasted from 1954 to 1962). He was reassigned in 1957 to the ''[[Commissariat à l'énergie atomique]]'' (CEA), for which he worked in Geneva from 1957 to 1958 at [[CERN]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Froissart |first=M. |year=1959 |title=Covariant formalism of a field with indefinite metric |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF02724848 |journal=Il Nuovo Cimento |language=en |volume=14 |issue=1 |pages=197–204 |doi=10.1007/BF02724848 |bibcode=1959NCim...14..197F |issn=0029-6341|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Again in civil cooperation with the French military, he was reassigned to work at the University of Algeria from 1958 to 1959.<ref name="CdF" /> He completed his study at Mines ParisTech in 1959.<ref name="ParisTechstudents" /> He held a temporary appointment from 1960 to 1961 at the [[University of California, Berkeley]],<ref name="CdF" /> where he worked on [[S-matrix]] theory under the leadership of [[Geoffrey Chew]]<ref>{{cite book | last=Frautschi | first=Steven |author-link=Steven Frautschi |title=A Passion for Physics | chapter=My experiences with the S-matrix program | publisher=World Scientific | year=1985 |doi=10.1142/9789811219207_0009 | pages=44–48| isbn=978-9971-978-29-7 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | editor=Brink, L. |editor-link=Lars Brink |editor2=Brower, R. C. | editor3=DeTar, C. | editor4=Tan, C. | editor5=Phua, K.K. |editor-link5=Phua Kok Khoo|chapter=''My Postdoctoral Years at Berkeley with Geoff Chew'' by Steven Frautschi|title=Geoffrey Chew: Architect Of The Bootstrap | publisher=World Scientific Publishing Company | year=2021 | isbn=978-981-12-1984-9 | chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KGxYEAAAQBAJ&pg=PA42 | access-date=2023-06-13 | pages=42–47}} (See p. 42.)</ref><ref name="Polkinghorne" /> and collaborated with, among others, [[Marvin Leonard Goldberger|Marvin "Murph" Goldberger]] and [[Kenneth M. Watson]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Froissart | first1=M. | last2=Goldberger | first2=M. L. | last3=Watson | first3=K. M. | title=Spatial Separation of Events in S-Matrix Theory | journal=Physical Review | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=131 | issue=6 | date=1963-09-15 | issn=0031-899X | doi=10.1103/physrev.131.2820 | pages=2820–2826| bibcode=1963PhRv..131.2820F | s2cid=123008336 | url=https://resolver.caltech.edu/CaltechAUTHORS:FROpr63 | url-access=subscription }}</ref> At [[Princeton University]], he held temporary positions for the academic years 1961–1962 and 1965–1966.<ref name="CdF"/> In the 1960s, he collaborated with the mathematician [[Bernard Morin]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Jackson, Allyn|title=The World of Blind Mathematicians|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |date=November 2002|volume=49|issue=10|pages=1246–1251|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200210/comm-morin.pdf}} (See p. 248.)</ref>

In 1964 Froissart received the [[Prix Paul Langevin]] awarded by the [[Société Française de Physique|''Société Française de Physique'' (SFP) ]].<ref name="SFP">[http://sfp.in2p3.fr/Prix/prix_anciens.html "List list of all SFP award recipients since the creation of the company, until 2002”], on the site sfp.in2p3.fr</ref> He contributed to the 13th International Conference on High-Energy Physics held in Berkeley from the 1st of August to the 7th of September 1966.<ref>{{cite book | author=U.S. Atomic Energy Commission | chapter=''Fundamental Theoretical Questions'' by M. Froissart|title=Proceedings of the XIIIth International Conference on High-Energy Physics, Held at Berkeley, California, August 31-September 7, 1966 | publisher=University of California Press | year=1967 | pages=13–25 |chapter-url= https://books.google.com/books?id=x-1AAQAAIAAJ&q=session+1+fundamental+theoretical+questions}}</ref> In January 1967 his paper with [[John R. Taylor]] was published.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Froissart | first1=Marcel | last2=Taylor | first2=John R. | title=Cluster Decomposition and the Spin-Statistics Theorem in S-Matrix Theory | journal=Physical Review | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=153 | issue=5 | date=1967-01-25 | issn=0031-899X | doi=10.1103/physrev.153.1636 | pages=1636–1648| bibcode=1967PhRv..153.1636F }}</ref> In October 1967 in Brussels, Froissart was an invited participant at the 14th Solvay Conference.<ref>{{cite book|author=Mehra, Jagdish|author-link=Jagdish Mehra|chapter=Chapter 12. Fundamental Problems in Elementary Particle Physics|title=The Solvay Conferences on Physics: Aspects of the Development of Physics Since 1911| page= 299|publisher=Springer|year=1975|isbn=9789401018678 |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jqXsCAAAQBAJ&pg=PA299}}</ref> In 1973 he was appointed a professor at the [[Collège de France]] in the particle physics chair, which he held until he retired as professor emeritus in 2004.<ref name="CdF"/>

[[File:College_de_france_pediment.jpg|thumb|left|upright|[[Pediment]] of the Collège de France, bearing the crest with the Latin motto ''Docet omnia'']]
Froissart consolidated into a single laboratory, dependent on his professorial chair, two laboratories — one headed by [[Francis Perrin (physicist)|Francis Perrin]] and the other by [[Louis Leprince-Ringuet]]. At the time of the consolidation, those laboratories were the two largest of the Collège de France.  The immediate task was to unify those two laboratories, whose members generally considered the two as competing organizations. A longer-term task was to reduce the size of the laboratory, while maintaining significant activity on the international scene. At the consolidated laboratory, the policy followed by the Collège de France was to only host small, easily mobile units — in case that the professor directing the consolidated laboratory was replaced by a new director pursuing different research goals in physics. Thus, in the consolidated laboratory, the physicists who wanted to work on the [[Large Hadron Collider|LHC]], which was not to enter service until after the departure of Professor Froissart, were jointly requested by the [[Institut national de physique nucléaire et de physique des particules|Institut national de physique nucléaire et de physique des particules (IN2P3)]] and the Collège de France to leave the consolidated laboratory and to join LHC-oriented laboratories. Of those researchers who remained in the consolidated laboratory, a majority turned to research on [[astroparticle]]s (to be in line with Froissart's expertise and leadership in high energy physics). The laboratory then took the name ''Physique corpusculaire et cosmologie'' (PCC). When Marcel Froissart retired, the laboratory formed the core of the new [[Astroparticle and Cosmology Laboratory]] (APC, ''AstroParticule et Cosmologie''), created in 2006 by [[Pierre Binétruy]]. The new laboratory had researchers from [[Paris Diderot University]] (Paris 7), the [[Paris Observatory|''Observatoire de Paris'']] and the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission|''Commissariat à l'énergie atomique'' (CEA)]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://apc.u-paris.fr/APC_CS/en/memoriam-pierre-binetruy-1955-2017 |title=In memoriam Pierre Binetruy (1955–2017)|website=Laboratoire Astroparticule & Cosmologie (APC)}}</ref>

[[File:Paris7 condorcet.jpg|thumb|Bâtiment Condorcet, headquarters of the physics department of [[Paris Diderot University]] (Paris 7), in the [[13th arrondissement of Paris]] ]]

Froissart, as laboratory director, found himself at the center of a controversy over the [[rubbiatron]].<ref>{{cite journal | journal = L'Humanité | url = https://www.humanite.fr/node/152603 | title = Crise au sein du laboratoire de physique corpusculaire du Collège de France (Crisis within the particle physics laboratory of the Collège de France) | date = 1997-03-03 | first1 = Pierre | last1 = Agudo }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url = http://hebdo.nouvelobs.com/hebdo/parution/p1683/articles/a55238-nucleaire_la_bataille_du_rubbiatron.html | first1 = Fabien | last1 = Gruhier | journal = Le Nouvel Observateur | title = Nucléaire : La bataille du rubbiatron (Nuclear: The Battle of the Rubbiatron) | number = 1683 | date = 1997-02-06 }}</ref> He was one of the main developers of the [[Groupement des scientifiques pour l'information sur l'énergie nucléaire]] (GSIEN, Association of Scientists for Information on Nuclear Energy).<ref>{{cite journal|author=Lévy-Lambert, Hubert|title=Marcel Froissart (53), un physicien dans son siècle|journal=La Jaune et la Rouge|date=14 June 2016 |issue=N<sup>o</sup> 716, Juin/Juillet 2016|url=https://www.lajauneetlarouge.com/marcel-froissart-53-un-physicien-dans-son-siecle/}}</ref>

The famous photographer [[Martine Franck]] made a portrait of Froissart.<ref>{{cite web|title=Marcel Froissart|website=polytechnique.org|url=https://1953.polytechnique.org/InMemoriam/Froissart/MarcelFroissart.html}} (with 1978 photo)</ref> Marcel Froissart was a grandson of the glassmaker {{ill|Antonin Daum|fr}} and a nephew of {{ill|Michel Froissart|fr}}, who was in the 1930s one of the designers of the wooden construction technique called ''froissartage''.<ref>{{cite web|title=What is Froissartage? {{!}} Bushcraft|publisher=SIKANA English|website=YouTube|date=September 1, 2017|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gPUu068BCFTs}}</ref><ref>To learn more about the Froissart family, see the book by {{cite book|author1=C. Dolphin|author2=P. Lebrun-Pézeral|author3=D. Poublan|date=1995|isbn=2-226-07605-0|publisher=[[Albin Michel]]|title=Ces bonnes lettres: Une correspondance familiale au XIX<sup>e</sup> siècle}} and the associated website {{cite web|title=Froissart, Damas (1852-1923), ses proches et sa famille|url=https://lettresfamiliales.ehess.fr/view/Froissart,_Damas_(1852-1923),_ses_proches_et_sa_famille}}</ref>

Upon his death in 2015, Marcel Froissart was survived by his widow, 3 sons, 2 daughters,<ref>{{cite web|title=Marcel Froissart|website=Geneanet|url=https://gw.geneanet.org/wikifrat?lang=en&n=froissart&oc=0&p=marcel}}</ref> and 10 grandchildren.<ref name=dansnoscoeurs/>

== Selected research achievements ==
*  Study of the polarization stability of polarized relativistic protons in a synchrotron, showing the existence of ''[[resonance]]'' energies leading to polarization reversal {{Harv|Froissart|Stora|1960}}
* Work on the theory of particle collisions, within the framework of the Mandelstam representation<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.123.1053|author=Froissart, Marcel|year=1961|title=Asymptotic Behavior and Subtractions in the Mandelstam Representation|journal=Physical Review|volume=123|issue=3|pages=1053–1057|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.123.1053|bibcode=1961PhRv..123.1053F |url-access=subscription}} (This paper (on the famous [[Froissart bound]]) has over 2000 citations.)</ref><ref>{{Harvsp|Omnès|Froissart|1963}}</ref>
* Research of a possible axiomatic justification of the Mandelstam representation {{Harv|Fotiadi|Froissart|Lascoux|Pham|1965}}
* Generalization of Bell's inequalities to various systems {{Harv|Froissart|1981}}
* Research on the application of the theory of analytic functions to the localization of a point on a plane surface ([[#Patent|Patent 1988]])
* Studies of various properties of light mesons {{Harv|Benayoun|Froissart|1989}}
